div.head: VI Atr 3
div.ab: K. ⁊ witena gerædnes is, þæt muneca gehwilc, þe ute of mynstre sy, ⁊ regoles ne gyme, do swa him þearf is:
⁊ witena gerædnes is, þæt muneca gehwilc þe ute of mynstre sy ⁊ regoles ne gyme, do swa him þearf is:
And witena gerædnes is, þæt muneca gehwilc, þe ute of mynstre sy, and regoles ne gyme, do swa him þearf is:
Und Verordnung der Witan ist, dass jeder Mönch, der ausserhalb des Klosters ist, indem er der Regel nicht achtet, handle, wie ihm noth thut:
And it is the ordinance of the witan that every monk who is outside his monastery, paying no heed to his rule, do what he needs to:
And the decree of the councillors is, that every monk who is out of a monastery and who is not observing a rule, shall do what is his duty, namely,
And the decree of the councilors is that each monk who is out of a monastery and not in compliance with his rule shall do what is necessary for him:
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

note.seg: Aus einem Befehl des Reichstags an die Mönche macht Paraphrast einen des Episkopats an die Klostervorsteher. Dem Worte deliquium gibt er die Bed. von delictum
The paraphrast turns an order of the national assembly to the monks into one of the episcopate to the heads of monasteries. He gives the word deliquium the meaning of delictum
The explanation given by the Latin paraphrase is: per proprium arbitrium egressus vel proprii reatu deliquii expulsus.
